subject: Information Theory
title: The One-Time Pad
description: A quick win: understand The One-Time Pad.

hook.text: XOR your message with a random key as long as the message. Shannon proved this is mathematically unbreakable.

buildup.text: The one-time pad achieves perfect secrecy: the ciphertext reveals zero information about the plaintext.

discovery.text: Every possible plaintext maps to the same ciphertext with equal probability. There's nothing to crack.

twist.text: The catch: the key must be truly random, used exactly once, and as long as the message. That's impractical at scale.

climax.text: The Washington-Moscow hotline used one-time pads. Perfect security for the highest-stakes messages.

punchline.text: Unbreakable by math. Impractical by logistics.

quiz.question: Why is the one-time pad rarely used in practice?
options: The key must be as long as the message and used only once
